newsitem.title: KENYA: Disappointed investors drag Nairobi bourse index.
newsitem.headline: Disappointed investors drag Nairobi bourse index.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index shed 40.49 points on Friday under the weight of investors disappointed by poor results released by the Standard Chartered Bank of Kenya, bourse officials said.
Turnover was posted at 30.047 million shilling on 664,658 shares compared to 24.240 million shillings on 566,508 shares on Thursday.
"Investors got a really rude shock because many of them were buying shares expecting to get a bonus issue," a bourse official said.

The bank posted a 1.149 billion shillings profit after tax for the year ended December 31, 1996 which was a marginal gain compared to 1.129 billion shillings last year. It announced a final dividend of 1.75 shillings per share.
"Everyone thought they would hit the two billion mark. The dividend they have given is unsatisfactory," a senior broker said.
Brokers said as a result investors traded cautiously, which pushed prices down.
Barclays Bank of Kenya shed three shillings to close at 114 while Uchumi Supermarket eased to 41.50 from 43.
Barclays Bank announced a profit of 2.477 billion shillings after tax and extraordinary item compared to 2.120 billion shillings last year. The bank will issue a final dividend of seven shillings.
Financial analysts said stiff competition from the 'smaller' financial institutions was stifling growth in the financial sector.

"The competition for accounts is great because the smaller banks give a more personalised service," a broker said. "I think what most banks will now have to do is find ways to cut down on costs -- otherwise they will remain in the two-billion region for a long time" he added.

A statement released by Standard Chartered quoting their chairman said: "The results were achieved despite operating in a depressed economy, a severely competitive environment and a massive restructuring programme designed to drastically improve customer service."
Bourse officials said their decision to withhold a proportion of profits as reserves had reduced the amount available to shareholders.
Housing Finance announced 253 million shillings profit after tax compared to 181 million shillings in the previous year. The finance house will issue a final dividend of 75 cents.
Kenya Commercial Bank eased to 98.40 from 98.50 while Jubilee Insurance closed at 44 from 47.25.
Kenya Breweries was unchanged at 62 while Sasini Tea & Coffee closed at 10.30 from 10.45.
The East African Development Bank EADB.NR corporate bonds traded 16 million shillings between 100.70 and 100.96 percent compared to 30 million shillings at 100.79 percent on Wednesday.
